newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch call money slips with liquidity ample.
newsitem.headline: Dutch call money slips with liquidity ample.

text.p: Dutch call money rates slipped to near the special advances level of 2.50 percent on Wednesday as liquidity in the market was ample.
"The market is not very short of liquidity at the moment and banks have been saving under the current credit quota," said one dealer.
Other dealers said the current allocation under the special advances still had enough to spare.
Call money rates dropped to a bid range of 2.50-2.56 percent versus 2.62 percent on Tuesday.

"The current advances pact with an ample allocation had too long a duration," said one dealer, adding the market had needed the 6.57 billion guilders allocation during the last few days. "But, it is ample now," he said.
Other rates remained unchanged. Three-month deposits were bid at 2.92 percent.
Dealers said guilder rates were likely to stay near the current level.
The guilder was a touch stronger against the mark at 112.145 per 100 marks from 112.155 yesterday.
